title: Return a new primitive value
summary: When a slice state is a number or string, its reducer returns the next value.
introduction: When a slice state is a number or string, its reducer returns the next value. Your task: Run the add reducer with a starting value of 7.
learningObjectives: Run the add reducer with a starting value of 7.
Explain the example for return a new primitive value

blocks.text: When a slice state is a number or string, its reducer returns the next value. A primitive cannot be changed like a draft object field.
Use a JavaScript project with @reduxjs/toolkit installed. React examples also need react-redux and React. These imports require your project build tool and are not available in the plain playground.
Read the code step by step

items: `createSlice` groups a state value and its reducer rules. Redux Toolkit also generates an action creator for each named reducer.

blocks.text: The reset reducer returns 0 from a previous state of 7.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Writing state++ without returning a primitive value does not correctly replace this number state.
